chapter: Ben Pollack band and New York
title: Glenn Miller the task master; woodshedding a hard part
summary: Miller refuses to simplify a tough arrangement and tells him to woodshed it; McPartland explains the term.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: And goodness gracious. But Benny was, now he was always for his family. He always saw that they were well taken care of. But he was quite frugal a good business man. An excellent business man. And Glen, Glen Miller, he was quite a guy. He was the task master. He used to arrange. And man I know that the Black Hearth there, he came in with an arrangement, we used to rehearse after the job. He came in there with an arrangement one night that we were going to record and there were some tough parts in there you know.
And I said, hey Glen, I said this is tough man this part. Can't you change it? He says, no. He says, take it home and woodshed it Jimmy. He said, it will make a better musician out of you.
He was right you know. What could I say. So I woodshedded the thing. I took it home and woodshedded it and we made the recording date and it came out good.
